reason: The microbes and undigested fibre occupy the same colon, suggesting a direct exchange to explore.
expectation: The microbes will use some of the undigested material and produce substances in the colon.

alternatives.reason: The mucus could first be connected to the colon lining.

effect: The microbes ferment some fibre into small fatty acids and gas, leaving other fibre behind. I can now connect these contents to the colon.
reaction: The distinction that not all microbes are helpful adds useful nuance.
reason: The fermenting contents are already in the colon, so combining them with the body may show their exchange with the host.
expectation: The colon will show how its lining interacts with the fermented contents.

alternatives.reason: The mucus could first be connected to the lining.

effect: The body now shows fatty acids entering lining cells and blood, alongside water and salt absorption; mucus remains to be connected.
reaction: The arrows make the host–microbe exchange clearer.
reason: The mucus comes from the colon lining, so it should connect directly to the body containing the microbes.
expectation: The mucus will form a layer between the colon lining and its contents.

effect: The completed colon model shows mucus separating most bacteria from the lining, alongside water and salt recovery and uptake of microbial fatty acids.
reaction: The combined cutaway makes the different exchanges easier to follow.

mostWorthwhile.text: Combining the fermenting contents with the body was most worthwhile: the planned illustration connected microbial products to uptake by colon cells and blood, as well as water and salt absorption.

leastWorthwhile.text: The final mucus addition was clear, but its protective role was mostly conveyed by the picture rather than explained in the brief prose.

surprise.text: The model showed that colon cells can use some fatty acids produced when bacteria ferment fibre, while others enter the blood.

arbitrary.text: No action felt particularly arbitrary; the items and their shared colon setting gave each combination a clear purpose.

continue.text: I would choose to continue: connecting microbial activity to the body's existing digestive and circulatory structures made the biology interesting, though the planned pictures alone do not establish how well students would understand it.
